Botteri's Sparrow (Peucaea botterii) is a medium-sized emberizid that occupies arid grasslands and scrublands of the southwestern United States and Mexico. The initial wet weight of the freshly laid egg is 2.75 grams [Ww0 = 2.75 grams], indicating that the female transfers substantial water content to the developing embryo. This brief nestling period is characteristic of many open-country sparrows, likely an adaptive response to high predation pressure.

The maximum reproductive rate is constrained by the short breeding window imposed by the hot, dry summer conditions. First breeding attempts are initiated relatively late in the season compared to other grassland sparrows, allowing females to accumulate sufficient body condition for egg production. Nest success is highly variable, with rates influenced primarily by predation from snakes and small mammals.
